Main focus: secure private access, egress controls, IP allowlisting, regional data residency, and whether Dedicated or Private (VPC) deployment is required. Security team flagged SOC2 evidence, KMS/HSM integration, and audit logs as gating items. Agreed to run an architecture workshop and share security pack and sample network diagrams.

transcript:
[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — excited to dig into Harborview's private access needs. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Dr. Priya Kapoor (Harborview): Priya here, infrastructure architect. Marcus from security will chime in.
[00:12] Marcus Lee (Harborview): Marcus, security. Hi.
[00:15] Liam (Redwood SE): Liam Chen, I'll handle the deep netting and architecture questions.
[00:19] Ellen Park (Harborview): Ellen, cloud engineer.
[00:23] Ava: Great. Agenda — we want to understand current network topology, any regional constraints, compliance gating items, and whether you need Dedicated reserved capacity or a VPC-private deployment.
[00:32] Priya: Our immediate blocker is that some of our models process EU patient metadata; workloads must stay in eu-west-1. We also want private egress — no public internet calls for inference.
[00:45] Marcus: From security: we need SOC2 evidence, proof of audit logs for inference traffic, customer-managed KMS support, and the ability to rotate keys. We also want to avoid hairpinning through the public internet.
[00:58] Liam: Understood. There are a few options — Redwood Private with PrivateLink/private endpoints, VPC peering, or using a Transit Gateway model. Each has tradeoffs for cross-account routing, IP planning, and egress controls.
[01:12] Ellen: Can you explain the egress options? We have strict egress ACLs and NAT gateway rules.
[01:18] Liam: Sure — shortest summary: 1) VPC peering allows direct routing between your VPC and Redwood's service VPCs — low latency but peer-to-peer scale can be an operational overhead if you have many accounts. 2) AWS PrivateLink (endpoint services) gives you private endpoints in your VPC and keeps traffic inside the AWS network — you don't need route table changes, but it requires ENIs and scales differently. 3) Transit Gateway is suitable if you centralize connectivity across many VPCs and on-prem via TGW attachments.
[01:47] Priya: We run multiple accounts and want a central model; Transit Gateway sounds appealing. What about static egress IPs? Our downstream firewall rules only permit a small set of IPs.
[01:58] Ava: Redwood can provision static outbound egress IPs per region for Dedicated/private deployments; for PrivateLink typically egress remains within the customer's VPC so outbound traffic uses your NAT or egress path. For Hosted, static egress IP is harder.
[02:15] Marcus: So if we pick PrivateLink, we still control egress because calls leave via our NAT?
[02:21] Liam: Correct, with PrivateLink your VPC initiates calls to the endpoint and any downstream egress is via your own routing. If we host inference in our VPCs and provide private endpoints, you can enforce egress with your own proxies/NAT.
[02:33] Ellen: Is there a required CIDR range we need to reserve? We have overlapping subnets across accounts.
[02:38] Liam: For VPC peering, we need non-overlapping CIDRs. For PrivateLink, less strict but we still need to plan ENI IPs; we'll provide a suggested CIDR pool. Liam: we'll send a suggested IP plan.
[02:50] Priya: How about cross-region failover? We must keep EU-data in EU but want DR in a separate EU site.
[02:58] Ava: We can pin model versions and region policies. For EU-only workloads we can route to eu-west-1 endpoints and keep data residency. For DR within EU, we can replicate models to eu-central-1 for failover, but there's a data residency and replication policy to sign off on.
[03:14] Marcus: Audit logs — do you provide per-request traces and token-level logs? We need to keep request IDs for 90 days.
[03:21] Liam: Redwood's Console has per-route tracing and request-level metadata. For Private deployments, logs can be forwarded to your logging endpoints (e.g. Splunk or S3 via Kinesis). We also support syslog/forwarding and can integrate with your SIEM.
[03:33] Marcus: And encryption at rest? KMS?
[03:36] Ava: We support customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS/HSM for model artifacts and encryption at rest in Private and Dedicated offerings. For Hosted, we have BYOK options but with different controls.
[03:48] Ellen: Any constraints around SAML SSO and RBAC? We need SCIM provisioning.
[03:53] Liam: We support SSO via SAML and SCIM for user provisioning and RBAC can be mapped to your roles. On Private, we can integrate with your IdP over the private network if needed.
[04:03] Priya: What's the expected latency if we put models in eu-west-1 and connect via PrivateLink?
[04:08] Liam: Latency should be within 10-20ms additional hops — depends on your infra. We'll run a benchmark. For Dedicated reserved capacity colocated in your region you'd see lower P95 token latency.
[04:19] Priya: Cost concerns — Dedicated is more predictable but more expensive. Hosted is cheaper but doesn't meet our egress/residency needs.
[04:27] Ava: Exactly the tradeoff — Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and SLA, Private/VPC deployments give data isolation. We'll structure a pilot quote comparing per-token and reserved plans.
[04:37] Marcus: One more blocker: we must have IP allowlisting for management plane access and control plane — can Redwood limit admin console access via static IPs or SAML-only?
[04:46] Liam: For Private we can restrict the control plane to your network endpoints; for hosted we provide IP allowlisting for admin access and SSO. We need to align on whether you want the Redwood console accessible from your VPC only or via an admin jump host.
[04:59] Ellen: Can we get a sample VPC peering diagram and a PrivateLink diagram?
[05:03] Ava: Yes, we'll share a set of diagrams and an IP allowlist template.
[05:08] Priya: Regarding legal/compliance — we need a Data Processing Addendum and clarity on sub-processing.
[05:14] Ava: We'll include the DPA and list of subprocessors in the security pack.
[05:18] Marcus: Performance test — we'd like to run a replay of 50 concurrent sessions with ~512-token sequences. Can Redwood run this in a staging env?
[05:27] Liam: Yes, we can do a load test on Dedicated trial capacity in eu-west-1. We'll need your representative prompts and the dataset (or a synthetic replica).
[05:35] Priya: Timeline — we have an internal compliance review next month. If Redwood can deliver security artifacts and a pilot within two weeks, we'll fast-track.
[05:44] Ava: Sounds reasonable. We can target workshop next week and pilot quote by end of week after.
[05:50] [silence/hum]
[06:02] Ellen: One operational question — IP rotation. If Redwood advertises static egress, how do you handle IP rotation for long-lived allowlists?
[06:10] Liam: We support a maintenance window where we announce IP rotations; for Dedicated we can maintain a static set for the contract term or provide BGP / NAT solutions for stable egress.
[06:20] Priya: What about customer-managed proxies? Could we front Redwood with our internal proxy cluster?
[06:26] Liam: Absolutely — that's a common pattern. You terminate TLS at proxy then route to Redwood via PrivateLink or peering. That also gives you full packet-level controls and egress logging.
[06:36] Marcus: How granular are audit logs? We want user and token-level correlation.
[06:41] Liam: Logs include request id, user id (if auth passed), model, token counts, latency. We can export full request metadata to your SIEM for retention policies.
[06:50] Priya: Any gotchas for multi-account setups?
[06:55] Ava: Account linkage and IAM mapping is key. We recommend a central networking account that owns the TGW or PrivateLink endpoints and then attach spoke accounts. We'll document steps in the workshop.
[07:05] Ellen: Are there egress cost implications we should be aware of?
[07:08] Liam: Egress costs depend on your cloud provider — if traffic remains in-region and within the cloud provider's private network, costs are lower. PrivateLink has ENI charges; TGW has attachment fees. We'll map that in the cost comparison.
[07:21] Priya: To confirm next steps: security pack, diagrams, workshop, and pilot quote.
[07:26] Ava: Yes. We'll also include the Dedicated sizing options and a sample SLA.
[07:32] Marcus: For the workshop, please include your SE and a network engineer who knows Transit Gateway setups.
[07:38] Liam: I'll own the network portion and bring a colleague if we need deeper TGW/BGP expertise.
[07:43] Priya: Great. Anything else?
[07:46] Ava: No, we'll close with a recap in an email with attachments. Thanks everyone.
[07:51] [meeting ends — note: recording will be shared]
